vectors.comment: one snapshot_push then a fresh read (cursor absent): delivers the snapshot with an empty delta tail, state=data, next_cursor=0 (a snapshot consumes no delivery-sequence slot -- PH0-D20)
vectors.name: initial_snapshot

vectors.comment: delta batches: snapshot then two deltas; a fresh read (cursor absent) delivers the snapshot plus both deltas as one contiguous tail, next_cursor=2 (snapshot resumes at 0 -- PH0-D20 -- so the two deltas land at 1 and 2)
vectors.name: delta_batches

vectors.comment: resume from a retained seq (success): a reader catches up to head=0 (a snapshot resumes at its pre-push base -- PH0-D20), holds; a new delta releases it with ONLY the incremental tail (no snapshot re-sent), no dup/no skip
vectors.name: resume_retained_seq_success

vectors.comment: resume from an expired seq (typed reset): a reader is at seq=0 (caught up right after the initial snapshot -- PH0-D20 -- before consuming the pushed delta), which is below a NEW snapshot that later re-bases the store at seq=1 (the delta folded in, retiring the old delta window); its next read cannot be served from retained deltas -> state=reset, reset_reason=retention_exceeded, with a fresh snapshot+tail attached so the reader recovers in-band (roadmap Sec 3.2)
vectors.name: resume_expired_seq_reset

vectors.comment: generation-change reset: the producer explicitly declares SwmrReset (e.g. datascad's query generation changed -- opaque to taut-shape, carried in `detail`) while a reader is held caught-up at epoch=0/head=0 (PH0-D20); reset increments the node epoch to 1 and answers immediately with state=reset, reset_reason=producer_requested, reset_detail=gen2, no snapshot/deltas, next_cursor ABSENT (no snapshot survives a reset -- PH0-D19) -- a typed announcement, not silence. A subsequent probe read (cursor absent, timeout_ms=0) then sees would_block until the producer pushes a fresh snapshot.
vectors.name: generation_change_reset

vectors.comment: two readers at different cursors: s1 resumes from seq=0 (the snapshot's own resume position -- PH0-D20; gets both retained deltas), s2 is a fresh subscribe (gets the snapshot plus both deltas) -- independent addressed responses, same underlying store
vectors.name: two_readers_different_cursors

vectors.comment: backpressure/retention-bound behavior: node constructed with max_deltas=2; a snapshot then two deltas are accepted, but a third delta_push is rejected (dropped, nothing appended) with SwmrDiagnostic{error, retention_bound_exceeded} -- the producer must SnapshotPush to continue (see dev-docs/AtomSwmrNotes.md)
vectors.name: backpressure_retention_bound

vectors.comment: writer-uniqueness violation: writer_id 'w1' binds on the first producer input; a delta_push from a DIFFERENT writer_id 'w2' is rejected (dropped, nothing appended) with SwmrDiagnostic{error, writer_conflict} -- the wire-level enforcement of writers=single (single-writer discipline). A subsequent read from w1's writer still shows only w1's content.
vectors.name: writer_uniqueness_violation

vectors.comment: a read with no timeout_ms on a caught-up swmr (nothing pushed yet) emits nothing; a later snapshot_push releases it with the snapshot (D1/D14 analogues)
vectors.name: held_read_released_by_delta

vectors.comment: read with timeout_ms=50 on a caught-up swmr (already at head=0, PH0-D20) emits SetTimer{1,50}; timer_expired{1} answers would_block with next_cursor recomputed via the canonical resolver, not echoed (PH0-D19) (D14/D16 analogues)
vectors.name: held_read_timer

vectors.comment: timer_expired for an already-answered token is a no-op (emits nothing) -- token 1 is answered by the first timer_expired; the second is late (D14 analogue)
vectors.name: late_timer_ignored

vectors.comment: a second read on the same stream drops the held first (unanswered) and cancels its timer; the new hold gets a fresh monotonic token (D5/D16 analogues)
vectors.name: supersede

vectors.comment: a snapshot then seal; a caught-up reader gets eof; held reads are answered eof by seal itself (D12 analogue)
vectors.name: seal_then_drain_eof

vectors.comment: close{} answers held reads closed and emits ProducerStop{closed}
vectors.name: close_clean

vectors.comment: close{error} answers held reads failed with the error attached and emits ProducerStop{failed}
vectors.name: close_failed

vectors.comment: repeated seal/close emit nothing new (D6 analogue)
vectors.name: idempotent_seal_close

vectors.comment: end_stream{s1} drops s1's held read (no response), cancels its timer; s2 is untouched
vectors.name: end_stream_mid_hold

vectors.comment: with stop_when=last_reader: s1 and s2 end -> ProducerStop{last_reader_gone} exactly on the >=1->0 transition (D6 analogue)
vectors.name: last_stream_producer_stop

vectors.comment: same script as last_stream_producer_stop, knob off -> no ProducerStop on last-reader-gone (D6 analogue)
vectors.name: stop_when_explicit_only

vectors.comment: seal, then a snapshot_push and a delta_push: both are dropped (nothing appended), each emits exactly one SwmrDiagnostic{warn, push_after_terminal}, and a subsequent read still sees the pre-seal state (D18/D19 analogue)
vectors.name: push_after_seal_warns

vectors.comment: after seal, a fresh subscribe (cursor absent) still reads the retained snapshot+deltas as data before eof; only a reader already caught up at head sees eof (D12 analogue -- terminal describes the producer, not the retained state)
vectors.name: terminal_still_readable

vectors.comment: a delta_push before any snapshot exists is rejected (dropped) with SwmrDiagnostic{error, delta_before_snapshot} -- a producer sequencing bug, not a benign race
vectors.name: delta_before_snapshot

vectors.comment: 56-F2 (swmr variant): a read with a SUPPLIED positioned cursor (epoch=0, seq=5, arbitrary -- no snapshot has ever been established, so no sequence position can be valid) and timeout_ms=50 still holds (there is nothing to resolve against, regardless of the claimed seq) and emits SetTimer{1,50}; timer_expired{1} answers would_block with next_cursor ABSENT -- via the canonical resolver (PH0-D19), never echoing the originally supplied seq=5
vectors.name: pre_snapshot_timed_cursor

vectors.comment: review F5-06b: SwmrResetReason.invalid_resume_seq has schema and code but no prior vector reached it. A snapshot then a delta bring head=1; a probe read with a cursor past head (seq=99, a position that never existed -- always a client bug, the engine is authoritative on seq) -> state=reset, reset_reason=invalid_resume_seq, with a fresh snapshot+tail attached, next_cursor=head=1
vectors.name: invalid_resume_seq_after_snapshot

vectors.comment: review F5-02 (PH0-D19): a held read whose ORIGINAL request had an absent cursor holds (no snapshot yet, no timeout_ms); a producer SwmrReset must NOT force-answer it `state=reset` (there is nothing to have been reset FROM) -- this step emits NOTHING for s1, which stays held; a later snapshot_push then releases it normally with the fresh data ("resolves with a fresh snapshot of the new state")
vectors.name: absent_cursor_hold_across_reset

vectors.comment: review F5-03/PH0-D24: a reader caught up at head=0 right after the first snapshot holds (no timeout_ms); a SECOND snapshot_push (a redundant re-assertion / compaction, same writer) does NOT advance head (PH0-D20: a snapshot consumes no delivery-sequence slot) so the reader's stored cursor is still exactly caught up -- this step emits NOTHING (the hold is untouched, no spurious `reset`); a follow-up probe at the same cursor confirms would_block, not reset
vectors.name: caught_up_survives_compaction_push

vectors.comment: the never-read variant of #18 (log 20b parity, review F5-06c): a swmr with no streams ever created never spuriously stops its producer; end_stream on an unknown stream is a no-op (D6)
vectors.name: never_read_no_stop

vectors.comment: review F5 Sec 8.9: close{} answers s1 closed and emits ProducerStop{closed}; a LATER end_stream{s1} still transitions reader-count >=1->0 (the stream entry is not removed by close) and emits a SECOND ProducerStop{last_reader_gone} -- ProducerStop is idempotent by design (D6), so this double-stop is intentional and cross-engine-consistent, previously unpinned
vectors.name: post_close_end_stream_double_stop

vectors.comment: 56-F4: a reader caught up at head=0 with timeout_ms=50 holds and emits SetTimer{1,50}; a delta_push releases it EARLY (before the timer fires) and must cancel the now-unneeded timer first -- SwmrCancelTimer{1} THEN the data SwmrReadResponse carrying the new delta
vectors.name: timed_early_wake_delta

vectors.comment: 56-F4: a reader caught up at head=0 with timeout_ms=50 holds and emits SetTimer{1,50}; seal releases it EARLY with eof and must cancel the timer first -- SwmrCancelTimer{1} THEN the eof SwmrReadResponse
vectors.name: timed_seal_cancels_timer

vectors.comment: 56-F4: a read with no snapshot yet and timeout_ms=50 holds and emits SetTimer{1,50}; close{} releases it EARLY with closed and must cancel the timer first -- SwmrCancelTimer{1} THEN the closed SwmrReadResponse THEN SwmrProducerStop{closed}
vectors.name: timed_close_cancels_timer

vectors.comment: 56-F4: a reader caught up at epoch=0/head=0 (positioned cursor, not absent) with timeout_ms=50 holds and emits SetTimer{1,50}; a producer SwmrReset increments epoch to 1, releases it EARLY with state=reset, and must cancel the timer first -- SwmrCancelTimer{1} THEN the reset SwmrReadResponse (reset_reason=producer_requested, reset_detail=gen2, next_cursor ABSENT per PH0-D19)
vectors.name: timed_reset_cancels_timer

vectors.comment: durable reset regression: a reader previously reached epoch=0/seq=1, then is between polls while the producer resets to epoch=1 with detail=gen2 and rebuilds a snapshot+delta whose seq values overlap at 0..1. A later read with the old epoch=0/seq=1 must receive state=reset with the retained producer reason/detail and the fresh epoch=1 snapshot+tail; sequence equality must never hide the reset. Re-reading at the returned epoch=1/seq=1 is caught up and would_block.
vectors.name: reset_between_polls_epoch_overlap
